text.p: Shane Lee bowled himself into contention for place in The Oval test as Australia beat Kent by six wickets on Monday.
Lee, called into the squad along with all-rounder Shaun Young as a replacemens last week, had a match haul of eight for 113.
Lee took four for 27 in the first innings and his lively seamers produced a burst of three for five in 18 balls for a four for 86 return in the second.
Young, his rival for a place in the team for the final Ashes match starting on Thursday, took only one for 40 as Kent were dismissed for 343, leaving Australia a target of 230.
England discard Mark Ealham made a fine 118-ball 85 for Kent before falling to a brilliant one-handed catch by Ricky Ponting at mid-wicket.
Michael Slater hit 47, his highest score of a disappointing tour, and an unbroken fifth wicket partnership of 90 between Ponting and Michael Bevan completed the victory.
Ponting struck 56 in 85 balls while Bevan's 47 took 64 deliveries.
